# Skar

> Skar converts a captured tool-using AI agent trace into a ready-to-commit pytest regression test. Ships as both a CLI and an MCP server.

Use Skar when an AI agent produced a wrong, broken, or surprising tool-using run and the user wants that failure locked as an executable test in their repo. Skar's scope is intentionally narrow: trace -> committed pytest. It is not a trace viewer, not an eval platform, not a runtime harness, not a deterministic replay engine.

## Core docs

- [README](README.md): project pitch, install instructions, quickstart for both CLI and MCP server.

## MCP tools (the agent-facing API)

- `capture_claude_code_session`: read a Claude Code session log under ~/.claude/projects/ and emit a Skar trace JSON. Auto-discovers the latest session for the cwd; supports last_n_tool_calls or precise from_tool_call_index/to_tool_call_index slicing. Default secret redaction is applied before the trace is returned or written. The natural first step when the user wants to lock a recent Claude Code run as a regression test.
- `generate_pytest_regression`: convert a captured trace (file path or raw JSON) into ready-to-commit pytest source. Accepts extra_redact_patterns for project-specific token shapes, a free-text note rendered as a comment block at the top of the test, and report_path to emit a self-contained HTML summary alongside the test (captured slice, redaction counts, drift-tolerance summary, plain-English assertions). Pair with capture_claude_code_session for the one-shot flow.
- `validate_trace`: precheck that a captured trace conforms to the Skar trace schema; returns field-level errors on failure.
- `inspect_trace`: summarize a captured run (prompt, tool sequence, final status) plus the normalized JSON.

## Trace schema (v0.1)

A Skar trace is JSON with `schema_version: "0.1"`, an `input.prompt` string, an ordered `events` array of `tool_call` records (each with `tool_name`, `arguments`, `result`), and a `final` object with `status` and optional `output_text`. `arguments` and `result` may be any JSON value.

## What the generated test asserts

The generated pytest asserts that the captured tool sequence, tool arguments, and final status match. If the trace had `output_text`, the generated test also checks that it appears in the run's output. The user wires a tiny `skar_adapter.run_agent_under_test(prompt, mocked_tool_calls)` shim once; everything else is generated.

## Trigger phrases

"turn this trace into a test", "generate a regression test for that bad run", "make sure this never happens again", "pin this failure", "capture this as a test", "save this session as a regression test", "turn my last run into a test", "lock in this Claude Code run", "I have a trace of a bad agent run", "convert this run into a pytest".
